title: CAFO: Feature-Centric Explanation on Time Series Classification

problem.claim: Identifying important features such as sensors for multivariate time series classification is difficult because of high dimensionality, complex temporal dynamics, and the need for domain-specific interpretation.

gap.claim: Existing multivariate time series explanation methods mainly identify important time periods and are less effective at identifying key features, leaving feature-centric explanation underdeveloped.

contributions.claim: CAFO is a feature-centric explanation and evaluation framework for multivariate time series classification that combines convolution, channel attention, a depth-wise separable channel attention module, and QR decomposition-based feature orthogonalization loss.
The framework develops metrics for evaluating global and class-specific feature importance.
The abstract reports that feature orthogonalization improves attention-distribution separability and refines and stabilizes feature-importance rankings.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe CAFO as a novel feature-centric explanation and evaluation framework for multivariate time series.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive empirical analyses on two public benchmarks and synthetic and self-collected real-world datasets designed to highlight class-wise discriminative features.
The authors report that CAFO is robust and informative for assessing feature importance in multivariate time series classification.
The authors state that the code is available in the linked GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Feature identification in multivariate time series classification is important but challenging.
Existing explanations emphasize important time periods rather than important features, motivating a complementary feature-centric perspective.
CAFO introduces channel attention, depth-wise separable channel attention, and QR-based feature orthogonalization.
Orthogonalization is reported to improve attention separability and feature-ranking stability, while additional metrics assess global and class-specific importance.
The framework is evaluated on public, synthetic, and self-collected datasets, with reported robustness and informative feature-importance assessments.

source_observation.claim: Time-centric explanations may identify important periods without adequately identifying important features.

interpretation.claim: Explanation systems for multivariate temporal data may benefit from treating temporal localization and feature attribution as complementary objectives.

application.claim: For multivariate time series classifiers, evaluate feature importance globally and by class alongside time-centric explanations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this complementarity generalizes beyond multivariate time series classification.

unknowns: Exact dataset names, sizes, baselines, and quantitative results are not provided.
The definitions and validation procedures for the proposed metrics are not provided.
Ablations, training details, and computational costs are not provided.
